summary: The execution-pair candidate job in callable-cli-release-prepare.yml runs tests/portable-workspace/release/test_execution_pair_release.py before `prepare`, and `preparePair` in eng/callable-cli-release.fsx refuses unless HEAD equals the source and `git status --porcelain` is empty (CALLABLE_CLI_RELEASE_REFUSED: pair source must be exact clean HEAD). Once that control imported eng/execution_pair_forward.py, Python wrote eng/__pycache__/*.pyc into the checkout and the root .gitignore did not ignore bytecode, so the 0.3.1 candidate run 41145398620 (source 8a211a49) refused after a successful check-profile and restore. Reproduced locally; fixed by Coordination PR 1089 (ignore __pycache__/ and *.pyc), whose merge commit 248cc92b became candidate source A and prepared successfully in run 41151871317. The original 0.3.0 path predates that import and never hit it. Lesson: any step before `prepare` that writes untracked, non-ignored files makes the candidate source dirty; only `prepare` checks cleanliness (check-profile and verify do not), and changing .gitignore moves main, so such a fix must land before the candidate source is chosen. Observation at the cited revisions; not a statement about other profiles.
title: Execution pair candidate preparation fails if an earlier step leaves untracked files
